question.text: AMFI (Association of Mutual Funds in India) is best described as:

answer.text: An association of all registered Asset Management Companies in the mutual fund industry
A statutory regulator with enforcement powers over mutual funds
A government body under the Ministry of Finance
A subsidiary of SEBI responsible for mutual fund oversight

explanation.text: The Logic: AMFI is the association of all registered Asset Management Companies. It registers mutual fund distributors, issues best-practice circulars, interacts with SEBI on industry matters, and can discipline distributors for violations of its Code of Conduct as applicable. The workbook explicitly states that AMFI is neither a regulatory body nor a Self-Regulatory Organisation (SRO). The Trap: Candidates often label AMFI an SRO because it issues codes and circulars. The workbook is explicit that AMFI is not an SRO; the statutory regulator of mutual funds is SEBI. Note: AMFI-registered distributors (with an ARN) are bound by AMFI's Code of Conduct; violations can affect their ARN, but rule-making authority over mutual funds rests with SEBI.
